title: Advisor E-mobility Development Partnership With the Private Sector
experience_raw: Senior (5+ years of experience)
raw_text: Vacancy Announcement Position Advisor E-Mobility Development Partnership with the Private Sector Project/ Cluster Developpp: Building Rwanda’s E-Mobility Workforce: Training- & Incubation Centre Employment contract period 01.10.2026 – 31.12.2027 Salary band 4 Location Kigali Application deadline 13.09.2026 A. Background The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH is a federally owned international cooperation enterprise for sustainable development with worldwide operations. The GIZ Office in Kigali covers GIZ’s portfolio in Rwanda and Burundi. GIZ Rwanda/Burundi implements projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, the European Union and other commissioning authorities in the following priority areas: Sustainable Economic Development; Good Governance; Climate, Energy and Sustainable Urban Development; Digital Transformation and Digital Economy; and regional projects in the Great Lakes Region. Rwanda is positioning itself as a regional leader in sustainable mobility, with government policy actively driving a shift away from fossil-fuel vehicles. The country's technical and vocational training system must address the new areas to provide skills for local technicians to maintain EVs: EV technology, battery diagnostics, or high-voltage safety - technical careers on emerging green jobs. Targeted vocational training would close the EV skills gap, improve employment prospects for Rwandan graduates, and create the technical foundation for Rwanda's e-mobility ambition. B. Main Tasks and Responsibilities Technical leadership for the joint implementation of the e-mobility develoPPP project in Rwanda including: Budget and expenditure planning, Project and contract management Joint project management with the project partner Stakeholder relations with project and technical partners, risk and conflict management Technical and financial monitoring of the project and regular reporting to the local GIZ team and develoPPP headquarters team. C. Required Qualifications, Competences and Experience 1. Qualifications and professional experience Master’s degree in business administration, Economics, International Development, Political Science, Social Science or other related field. Minimum of 5 years’ experience in relevant thematic areas of the project, such as private sector development, TVET and related areas In-depth experience of working with or within the private sector management level Knowledge of skills development concepts and instruments, Train-of-Trainer concepts, Work experience in GIZ projects. Good knowledge of the Rwandan private sector landscape Effective project management skills and experience in complex multi-faceted projects. Ability to lead and work in a dynamic and multidisciplinary team and context. D. How to apply Interested candidates should submit their application (motivation letter, updated CV, certificates and references) via our electronic job portal by using the button “apply”; until 13th September 2026 at 4:00 PM. All attachments should be put together in one PDF file not larger than 2 MB. The cover letter should be limited to one page and the CV to a maximum of two pages. Otherwise, the application will not be considered. If qualified national candidates are identified, priority will be given to national candidates under an NMA contract. Applications are assessed on a rolling basis as they are received. Early application is therefore encouraged, as the recruitment process may be concluded before the stated deadline. GIZ is a signatory of the Diversity Charter. Recognition, appreciation and inclusion of diversity in the company are important to us. All employees shall be valued - regardless of gender and gender identity, nationality, ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, social background, age or sexual orientation. We support equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities. This includes the provision of reasonable accommodation, if needed, in order to participate in the job application and interview process and to perform essential job functions. Please let us know, if you have any particular requirements should you be invited for assessment/interview or that you wish us to consider, when considering your application. Women and persons with disabilities are particularly encouraged to apply. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for test and interview. GIZ Office Rwanda KN 41 St. / Nr.17, Kiyovu P.O. Box 59, Kigali, Rwanda GIZ reserves all rights! Apply

title: Chief Strategy Officer
industry_raw: Administration, Economics, Engineering, Finance and investment
experience_raw: Executive level
raw_text: Aviation Travel & Logistics Holding Ltd invites qualified, experienced, and visionary leaders to apply for the position of Chief Strategy Officer (CSO). The successful candidate will lead the Group’s strategic agenda and provide executive leadership in corporate strategy, business growth, portfolio management, investments, strategic partnerships, transformation, and performance management across ATL and its subsidiaries. Job Title:Chief Strategy Officer (CSO) Reports To:Chief Executive Officer Job Level:C-Level Employment Type: Full-Time Location:Kigali, Rwanda 1. Job Purpose The Chief Strategy Officer (CSO) will lead ATL’s enterprise-wide strategy development, strategic planning, corporate performance management, growth initiatives, investment evaluation, strategic partnerships, and transformation programmes. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the role will work closely with the Board, executive leadership, and subsidiary management teams to drive sustainable growth, long-term value creation, operational excellence, and effective execution of ATL’s strategic objectives across aviation, logistics, travel, training, infrastructure, and related business portfolios. 2. Key Duties & Responsibilities; a. Group Strategy & Strategic Planning Lead the formulation, execution and regularrefresh of ATL Holding’s strategy, ensuring alignment with shareholder expectations, market realities and long-term enterprise priorities. Translate the Group vision into clear strategic priorities, measurable objectives and practical execution plans across ATL and its Strategic Business Units. Define and refine strategic priorities, key initiatives and performance measures that guide executive decision-making and strengthen business accountability. Lead the annual strategic planning cycle and facilitate executive strategy discussions across the Group. Embeda consistent strategy planning framework and governance discipline across all Strategic Business Units. b. Strategy Execution & Transformation Leadenterprise-wide strategic initiatives, transformation programmes and priority projects from concept to delivery. Establish clear governance, milestones, accountabilities and performance measures for major strategic initiatives. Work with business leaders to resolvedelivery barriers, accelerate execution and maintain focus on strategic priorities. Convert strategic priorities into well-resourced execution plans aligned with capabilities, investment choices and performance expectations. Trackexecution progress and recommend timely corrective actions where performance or delivery falls behind approved plans. c. Business Development, Growth & Portfolio Management Identify and advance growth opportunities across aviation, airports, travel, logistics, training and adjacent sectors. Assess acquisitions, joint ventures, partnerships, investments and new ventures with strong strategic and commercial judgement. Oversee due diligence, market assessments, business cases and investment analysis to support sound executive decisions. Advise the CEO, CFO, business leaders, Boards and external advisors on investment and portfolio decisions. Monitor portfolio performance and recommend expansion, restructuring, optimisation or exit options that support long-term value creation. d. Market Intelligence & Strategic Advisory Provide forward-looking market intelligence to inform strategy across aviation, travel, logistics and related sectors. Lead market research, competitor analysis, scenario planning and review of emerging trends, technologies and regulatory developments. Assess external developments that may affect ATL’s strategy, competitive position, operating model and growth agenda. Develop strategic options that mitigate emerging risks and position the Group to capture high-value opportunities. Advise on business models, market entry, growth strategies, partnerships and major investment decisions. e. Financial, Investment & Business Case Analysis Partner with the CFO and business leaders to ensure strategic plans are supported by sound financial assumptions, capital requirements and sustainable business models. Review and challenge business cases, financial models, investment proposals and strategic project plans to strengthen decision quality. Support financial scenarios, capital planning and long-term projections for priority strategic initiatives. Ensure major strategic proposals demonstrate clear strategic alignment, commercial viability, risk discipline and expected returns. Support Group funding, investment and restructuring strategies in close collaboration with the CEO and CFO. f. Performance Management & Strategic Reporting Establish and oversee Group strategic performance measures, business objectives and executive-level performance indicators. Lead regular strategic and business performance reviews with the CEO and business leaders to reinforce accountability and delivery focus. Provideexecutive reporting on strategy execution, portfolio performance, growth opportunities and key performance trends. Strengthen reporting tools and processes to improve transparency, accountability and executive decision-making. Identify performance gaps and work with accountable leaders to drive timely corrective action. g. Corporate Communications & Strategic Positioning Lead the Group’s corporate communications and strategic positioning agenda, ensuring ATL’s external narrative reflects its strategy, vision and growth ambition. Shape and protect ATL’s corporate reputation with government, shareholders, investors, industry partners, media and other strategic stakeholders. Advise the Group CEO and Board on executive communications, stakeholder messaging, reputation matters and communications risks. Lead communication of major strategic initiatives, investments, partnerships, transformation programmes and corporate milestones. Oversee executive and external communications, media engagement and issues management to strengthen ATL’s visibility, credibility and sector influence. h. Strategic Partnerships & Stakeholder Engagement Develop strategic partnerships with governments, investors, financial institutions, aviation partners, development institutions and industry stakeholders. Represent ATL at strategic, industry, investment and business forums as delegated by the CEO. Build relationships that strengthen ATL’s market position, investment pipeline, strategic influence and access to critical capabilities. Coordinate with shareholder representatives and relevant government institutions on strategic matters through the Group CEO. Support clear communication of ATL’s strategic direction to employees, subsidiaries, partners, investors and other stakeholders. i. Governance & Executive Decision Support Provide strategic counsel to the Group CEO, Board and relevant Board Committees on major corporate, investment and portfolio decisions. Ensure strategic initiatives are supported by appropriate governance, business cases, accountability mechanisms and decision rights. Facilitate executive discussions thatstrengthen alignment, prioritisation and coordinated execution across the Group. Champion a culture of strategic discipline, accountability, innovation and high performance across the Group. Anticipate strategic risks and recommend mitigation measures or alternative strategic options. 3. Desired Profile a. Qualifications & Experience Master’s degree in Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Strategy, Engineering, Project Management or a related discipline. Relevant executive or professional qualifications are an advantage. At least 15+ years of progressive experience in strategy, business development, investment, transformation or a related field, with significantsenior leadership exposure. Proven track record of shaping and executing corporate strategies, growth agendas, transformation programmes and major strategic initiatives. Strong experience in investment evaluation, portfolio management, strategic partnerships and business case development. Experience in aviation, travel, logistics, infrastructure or another complex, regulated or multinational environment is highly desirable. b. Core Competencies Strategic Leadership & Corporate Strategy Business Growth, Development & Portfolio Management Commercial, Investment & Financial Acumen Market Intelligence, Strategic Risk & Foresight Transformation & Strategy Execution How to Apply Interested candidate should submit their application no later than 05th October 2026. Please click on the “Apply” button to complete your application. Interested candidates should also submit their application including an application letter, updated curriculum vitae, copies of academic and professional certificates, and any other relevant supporting documents through the official recruitment channel indicated by ATL. Applications should clearly indicate the position applied for: Chief Strategy Officer (CSO). Equal Opportunity Statement ATL is an equal opportunity employer. Recruitment will be conducted on the basis of merit, competence, leadership experience, and alignment with the requirements of the position. Apply

title: Marketing Associate, Acquisition
experience_raw: Mid career (3 to 5 years of experience)
raw_text: MAA JOB DESCRIPTION Position: Marketing Associate, Acquisition Reports to: Head of Marketing and Sales Location: Kigali (Rwanda) Expected Start Date: October, 2026 Apply by: Rolling, applicants are encouraged to state their interest early About Numida: Numida exists to help ambitious African small business owners achieve their dreams throughaccessible, digital financial services. Traditional lenders have failed this market, so since 2021 we’vebuilt a fast, fair and convenient working capital product that has disbursed more than $170M to over 118,000 businesses across East Africa. Our vision is to enable 1 million African small business owners to achieve their dreams by 2030. Toachieve this we are executing our mission of building financial products to catalyze meaningful change for ambitious African small business owners and their communities. We are Uganda’s first YC-backed fintech and one of Africa’s fastest-growing technology companies. We are expanding rapidly across the region and building products that deeply serve entrepreneurs in meaningful, practical ways. Find out more at https://numida.com. About the role: We launched in Rwanda in 2026, and the business has grown every month since. The market is responding well, and the team is scaling behind it. What we are missing is a dedicated marketing presence on the ground. Work planned centrally hasconsistently taken longer to reach the market than it should, and content, media partnerships and Kinyarwanda copy have all waited on shared capacity. This role changes that. You would be our first marketing hire in Rwanda, which means real ownership from the first week anda genuine hand in how Numida shows up in this market. Strategy is shared. You will help shape italongside the Head of Marketing and Sales and the central marketing team, and your read on the market will carry real weight. Where the accountability sits with you is delivery. Where your focus sits This is a generalist role, and we want to be clear about that from the start. Around 70 percent of your time sits with acquisition marketing for Rwanda. That is your home, and it is what we are hiring you for. The remaining 30 percent goes to wider marketing priorities across the department. We are a small team covering three markets at different stages, so priorities move. In practice, that might mean supporting a campaign running in another market, helping a product launch land locally, contributing to team-wide research, or covering a colleague during a busy period. It is shared work, and everyone in the team carries some of it, including your manager. We put this in writing because it is real. If you would prefer a role with a fixed, unchanging remit, this is probably not the right fit. If you like variety and enjoy being useful across a function, you will do well here. MAA JOB DESCRIPTION What you will own 1. Content and community The monthly content calendar across our social channels, in both English and Kinyarwanda. Building, scheduling and publishing content. Community management in conjunction with customer care. Most inbound messages ask how to apply or what is happening with an application, so responding well and routing quickly to sales makes a direct difference. Kinyarwanda copy. You will either write it or own the native speaker review before anything is published. Getting the language right is one of the most valuable things this role does. 2. Paid and earned media Media and publisher partnerships, including briefing newsrooms and checking compliance language before anything runs. Radio and broadcast scheduling, covering booking, script approval and confirming that spots aired as agreed. The influencer and creator programme. Sourcing, briefing, contracting, attribution and a monthly view of what each creator delivered. 3. Client stories and assets Finding clients who are happy to share their story publicly, in their own language. Consent and image release forms completed before any filming or photography. As a regulated lender this matters to us and to our clients. Scheduling shoots and getting usable assets back on time. 4. Direct channels and sales support SMS, in app and WhatsApp campaigns, from defining the audience through to reporting back. Assets for the sales team, including banners, flyers and agent talk tracks, written in Kinyarwanda first. 5. Budget and administration Tracking spend against the Rwanda marketing budget, and handling vendor contracting, invoicing and payment follow-up. How the role runs Monday. The week is confirmed, and the assets are ready to go. Midweek. A performance read covering spend, leads and results by source. Friday. The following week is drafted and in review. Late in each month. The month ahead is agreed and locked. How performance is reviewed We reviewed four things. The specific measures are agreed with your manager when you join and revisited each quarter, so they stay relevant as the business moves. Business impact. The commercial result your work contributes to in your market or area. Delivery. Whether work reaches the market when it was planned to, and whether the budget is used as intended. MAA JOB DESCRIPTION Efficiency. Whether the cost of the results you produce improves over time. Collaboration. How well you work with sales, data and the rest of the marketing team, and how well you share what you learn. Delivery carries real weight here. Work that reaches the market on schedule and teaches us something is worth more to us than perfect work that arrives late. Your first 90 days These are milestones rather than targets. We are looking for early signs that you can hold work together and make sense of a new environment. You understand our clients, our products and our numbers well enough to have your own opinions about them. The work you own is running to a plan that other people can see, with the dates being met. Your key relationships are in place, inside the team and with the partners and vendors you rely on. You have brought us at least one idea we had not thought of, based on something you observed rather than general best practice. What we are looking for Around two to four years of hands-on marketing execution, from an agency, startup, telco, financial services or FMCG background. Kinyarwanda as a first language. You will be writing in it, reviewing it and making judgement calls about tone in it. Experience running things end to end. Booking the media, following up the invoice, being present at the shoot and pulling the report afterwards. Breadth. You are comfortable moving between copy, content, media, events and sales support in the same week. Organisation that other people can see. Clear calendars, trackers and files. Enough ease with numbers to read a performance dashboard and explain what it means. What would help you stand out Experience in financial services or another regulated sector. Having been the first or only marketing person somewhere. Design, photography or video skills, even at a basic level. Is this role right for you? This is a hands-on, broad role in a market we are still building. If you like ownership, variety and being the person who makes things happen, it will suit you well. If you are looking for a role focused mainly on strategy with execution handed to an agency, this is not that role, and we would rather be upfront about it. Sharing what you build Keeping your work visible to the wider team is part of the job rather than an extra. We will ask you to maintain a working playbook for what you own, a vendor and partner list with rates and contacts, and records of what you ran and what came of it. This protects you as much as it protects us. It makes leave, handovers and growth in the team far easier for everyone. MAA JOB DESCRIPTION How we work together You report to the Head of Marketing and Sales, who sets your priorities. You will work hand in hand with the Rwanda sales team. This is a partnership rather than a reporting line, and marketing remains your home. A weekly check-in with your manager. Short, direct and focused on what shipped and where you need support. Why this role is worth taking Real ownership. You will run things end to end rather than support someone else running them. Breadth. Three markets, several products, and a marketing function still being built, which is unusual exposure at this level. Proximity. You report directly to the Head of Marketing and Sales, so there is a short line between your work and the decisions it informs. Room to grow. The team is expanding, and people who do well here take on more, quickly. Why Join Numida? You will play a major role in shaping the next era of operations at Numida. You will join a mission-driven team transforming access to finance for African entrepreneurs. You will work with smart, caring people who value clarity, ownership and teamwork. You will receive competitive compensation, a flexible hybrid environment and strong opportunities for growth and leadership development. How to apply Send your CV and a short note telling us about one piece of work you delivered from start to finish, including what worked, what did not, and what you would do differently. We are more interested in that than in a formal cover letter. Applications to https://forms.gle/9LwsJ2atTzNFGVor9 . We review on a rolling basis and will come back to every applicant. Numida is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from everyone, and we make our hiring decisions on merit. If you need any adjustments to the process, tell us, and we will arrange it. Attachment attachment_file_5389a8b4173b17935391 Apply

raw_text: Job Title: Project Assistant (3 Vacancies) Department/Group: Implementation Reporting To: Project Officer Years of Experience 2+ Years Location: Rutsiro (2) and Nyamasheke (1) Travel Required: 90% Job description About Raising The Village At Raising The Village (RTV), we are dedicated to eradicating ultra-poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa. As a dynamic, rapidly growing international development organization, we’ve assembled a team of over 350+ passionate individuals in Uganda, Rwanda, DRC and Tanzania, alongside an additional 15+ professionals in North America. Together, we are committed to elevating communities out of ultra-poverty by implementing innovative solutions and leveraging advanced data analytics to drive impact. To date, our holistic approach has positively impacted over 1,000,000 lives since 2012, and we’re poised to achieve even greater milestones, aiming to assist 1 million individuals annually by 2027. Our growth and success are fueled by the invaluable support of global partners who share our vision of sustainable change. Learn more about our impactful programs at www.raisingthevillage.org Position Summary Role and Responsibilities Project Implementation Conduct project design review meetings with respective partner villages and provide feedback as required to update project designs and budgets prior to implementation; Coordinate training activities including but not limited to financial literacy and behavior and mindset change, water and health sanitation, village savings and loans associations, agriculture, livestock care and management, etc. Responsible to implement RTV’s project methodologies with the purpose of increasing household income and reducing extreme poverty as per project designs; Develop and submit list of required goods and services for project implementation to the procurement and logistics officer; Responsible to verify goods/inputs prior to distribution; Conduct project follow-up and provide support and guidance to community groups and individual households to ensure project compliance continuation. Identify potential risks and issues and provide mitigation measures and recommendations for improvements; Conduct regular meetings with leadership and community members on performance, participation, and perceptions of RTV based projects. Government & Community Coordination and Support Build and maintain strong working relationships with Cell-level government officials (SEDOs and Executive Secretaries) to support day-to-day RTV program activities. Work closely with community leadership and support structures including Inteko z’abaturage, Incuti z’umuryango, Abajyanama b’Ubuzima, Abajyanama b’Ubuhinzi (farmer promoters), para-social workers, community coaches, technical and village coaches, and other community actors to ensure their active participation in RTV programs. Mobilize households and communities for trainings, meetings, and program activities to promote clear understanding, strong participation, and adoption of RTV program components. Assist in delivering trainings to community and cell-level actors on RTV program methodology, M&E processes, technology use, and field protocols, under the guidance of the Project Officer or Project Manager. Provide on-the-job support and follow-up to community and government actors during implementation to help address challenges and encourage consistent participation. Promote positive collaboration and trust between RTV staff, government officials, and community structures to strengthen community ownership and contribute to sustainable program impact. Reporting and Administration Develop and manage work plans; Complete field reporting on a weekly basis and provide support with information sharing for donor reporting and proposal writing as might be required; Attend and participate in weekly staff meetings as well as cluster team meetings to highlight issues and success and outline next steps; Complete weekly financial request, submissions and accountabilities to the Project Officer; Take photographs and share them for data repository. Monitoring and Evaluation: Support field monitoring activities such as attendance tracking, basic data collection, household follow-ups, and reporting using RTV tools and systems. Providing feedback and recommendations to the Project Officer and Project Manager, and the program team to improve RTV’s way of work; Provide suggestions to management on potential activities that need to be redone, reviewed or introduced to ensure sustainability of RTV projects, methodologies, and improvement in the lives of community members. Note: Other requirements might be required by their direct supervisor and/or management. Preferred Qualifications and Experience Education and Experience: Bachelor’s degree in social science, Social Work, Humanities, Community Development, or related field of study Bachelor’s degree in agriculture is preferred but not required Minimum of two (2) years of relevant work experience at the village level Demonstrated experience working with and coordinating local government institutions and officials, particularly at Sector and Cell levels (mandatory) Preferred Skills if any Strong training & facilitation skills; Strong communication skills, both verbal and written English; Fluent in local languages where RTV works; Proficiency in Microsoft Office programs i.e. Word and Excel Understanding of Community Based Development Principles Organizes work effectively while remaining aware of changing priorities and deadlines; Able to work independently to accomplish tasks, but also as part of a team to achieve mutual goals and objectives; Able to think outside of the box to provide plausible solutions to issues and challenges; Strong work ethic, flexible, and able to build relationships with various stakeholders most notably colleagues, and community members; Able to keep a positive attitude in a fast-paced and challenging environment; Energetic and physically able to hike high to hike high terrain; Able to travel approximately 90% of time; Ability to ride a motorbike with a valid Rwandan rider’s permit (class A) and demonstrated experience navigating remote, rural and hilly terrain (mandatory). We encourage women, people with disabilities and minority groups to apply for this position. RTV is committed to equal opportunities and diversity of perspective at the workplace. Disclaimer: Raising the Village DOES NOT charge any kind of FEE(s) at whichever stage of the recruitment process. Attachment attachment_file_5d3e69aca669c1ff8f52 Apply

title: Architect
experience_raw: Senior (5+ years of experience)
raw_text: Aviation Travel & Logistics Holding Ltd invites qualified, competent, and motivated candidates to apply for the position of Architect. The role will support the planning, design, coordination, and delivery of aviation and airport infrastructure and facilities across ATL projects, including logistics, travel, infrastructure, and related development projects. Job Title:Architect Reports To:Senior Site Engineer Job Level:Specialist Employment Type:Full-Time Location:Kigali/Bugesera, Rwanda 1. Job Purpose The Senior Architect will provide senior-level professional technical expertise and leadership in the planning, design, coordination and delivery of aviation and airport infrastructure and facilities across ATL projects, including logistics, travel, infrastructure and related development projects. The role will ensure that all architectural and engineering solutions are technically sound, operationally fit for purpose and compliant with applicable laws and regulations, approved project requirements, safety standards, quality requirements and sustainability objectives. The position will work as part of multidisciplinary project teams, coordinating with designers, consultants, contractors, regulators, stakeholders and other technical specialists to support the successful delivery of ATL projects to the required quality, cost, schedule, safety and performance standards. The Senior Architect will also provide technical leadership, direction and mentorship to project architects and design staff, and may deputise for senior technical leadership on aviation and airport infrastructure matters as required. 2. Key Duties & Responsibilities; a. Architectural & Engineering Design Develop, review and coordinate architectural designs, drawings, specifications, calculations and technical documentation for ATL facilities and infrastructure. Ensure designs are aligned with airport operational requirements, ICAO standards, applicable building codes, technical standards and approved project specifications. Review design proposals, technical submissions and design changes, providing professional recommendations on functionality, safety, constructability, cost and sustainability. Support the development of technically robust and cost-effective solutions throughout the project lifecycle. Provide senior technical leadership, direction and mentorship to project architects, designers and technical staff engaged on ATL aviation and airport infrastructure projects. b. Infrastructure & Multidisciplinary Coordination Coordinate technical interfaces across terminal facilities, airside infrastructure, landside facilities, utilities, cargo, passenger processing, support facilities and associated infrastructure. Facilitate effective coordination between architectural, civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, ICT, aviation systems and other specialist disciplines. Identify and resolve technical interfaces, design conflicts and coordination issues that may affect project delivery. Ensure airport operational, passenger experience, safety, security and maintainability requirements are incorporated into technical solutions. c. Project Delivery & Technical Oversight Monitor the implementation of approved designs, drawings, specifications and technical requirements during construction. Conduct site inspections and technical reviews to verify compliance with approved designs, quality standards and project specifications. Review contractor submissions, method statements, shop drawings, material proposals, technical queries and requests for information. Identify technical deviations, construction challenges and emerging issues and recommend timely corrective actions. d. Aviation Standards, Safety & Regulatory Compliance Ensure technical solutions comply with applicable ICAO Standards and Recommended Practices (SARPs), Rwanda Civil Aviation Authority requirements, national building regulations and relevant international standards. Incorporate aviation safety, security, accessibility, fire and life safety, environmental and operational requirements into design and project delivery. Support regulatory reviews, approvals, inspections and technical engagements with relevant authorities. Promote a strong culture of technical integrity, safety, compliance and quality throughout the project. e. Quality, Cost, Risk & Change Management Support technical quality assurance and ensure that construction and design activities meet approved standards and specifications. Identify technical, design, construction and interface risks and support the development and implementation of mitigation measures. Review technical aspects of variations, claims, cost proposals and design changes and provide professional recommendations. Support value engineering and cost optimisation initiatives without compromising safety, quality, functionality or long-term asset performance. f. Testing, Commissioning & Handover Support testing, commissioning, inspection and acceptance of completed facilities, systems and infrastructure. Participate in snagging, defects identification, rectification and close-out activities. Review as-built drawings, operation and maintenance documentation and other technical handover requirements. Support the transition of completed facilities into safe and efficient airport operations. g. Technical Reporting & Documentation Maintain accurate technical records, drawings, specifications, inspection reports, approvals and project documentation. Prepare technical progress reports, design review reports, site inspection reports and recommendations for project leadership. Track technical deliverables, design approvals, outstanding issues and corrective actions. Ensure appropriate document control and traceability of technical decisions throughout the project lifecycle. h. Stakeholder & Professional Coordination Work closely with ATL project leadership, airport operators, government institutions, regulators, consultants, contractors and other technical stakeholders. Participate in design reviews, technical coordination meetings, site meetings and project governance forums. Provide professional technical advice and communicate complex technical matters clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Represent the project professionally in technical engagements as delegated by project leadership. 3. Desired Profile a. Qualifications & Experience Bachelor's degree in Architecture, Architecture Engineering, or a related discipline; a Master's degree is an added advantage. Professional registration with the relevant regulatory body and a valid practising licence, where applicable, is required. Minimum of 5 years' relevant experience in architecture, engineering, infrastructure development, construction, or major capital projects, including prior experience operating at a senior or lead technical level. Proven experience in the delivery or supervision of large-scale aviation, airport, transportation, infrastructure, commercial, or other complex capital projects. Strong knowledge of design development, multidisciplinary coordination, construction supervision, technical assurance, quality control, and applicable international technical standards. Demonstrated experience providing technical leadership, guidance and mentorship to architects, engineers and multidisciplinary design teams on complex capital projects. b. title: Umushoferi
experience_raw: Not specified
raw_text: ITANGAZO RY’AKAZI N’AMAHIRWE MGK – GUPATANA PROGRAM Aho ibikorwa bibera: Kigali, Rwanda Ikigo: MGK Umwanya: Umushoferi – Gupatana Andi mahirwe: Marketing Volunteers KURI MGK MGK ni ikigo gikora mu bijyanye na transport, gukodesha no gucunga imodoka, kikaba gitanga amahirwe ku bantu bafite ubushake bwo gukora no kwiteza imbere binyuze muri gahunda ya Gupatana. MGK irashaka abantu bafite ubunyamwuga, ubunyangamugayo, ubushake bwo gukora ndetse n’ubwitange kugira ngo bifatanye n’iyi gahunda. 1. ABASHOFERI BIFUZA KWITABIRA GUPATANA IMODOKA NO GUKORA MARKETING VOLUNTEERING MGK irashaka abashoferi bifuza kwinjira muri gahunda ya Gupatana, aho umukandida wujuje ibisabwa ashobora guhabwa imodoka yo gukoresha mu rwego rwa transport, hakurikijwe amasezerano n’amabwiriza bya MGK Cyangwa ushobora gukora ubukorerabushake mu mwuga wa transport (volunters) Ibisabwa ku mushoferi Umukandida agomba: Kuba afite uruhushya rwo gutwara ibinyabiziga rufite agaciro, cyane cyane icyiciro B cyangwa C. Kuba azi gutwara imodoka neza kandi afite uburambe mu gutwara. Kuba azi neza imihanda n’uduce dutandukanye twa Kigali. Kuba ari umuntu w’umunyakuri, wizerwa kandi ufite inshingano. Kuba yiteguye kubahiriza gahunda yo gukora no kwishyura hakurikijwe amasezerano. Kubahiriza amabwiriza ya MGK ajyanye no gukoresha, kubungabunga no kwita ku modoka. Kuba azi kuvugana neza n’abakiriya no gutanga serivisi nziza. Kuba yiteguye gutanga ibyangombwa n’amakuru bisabwa mu gihe cyo gusaba. AMAHIRWE YA GUPATANA Abashoferi bujuje ibisabwa bashobora kwinjira muri gahunda ya Gupatana, batangiriye ku deposit ya 1,000,000 RWF, hakurikijwe ibisabwa n’amasezerano ya MGK. Gahunda igamije guha umushoferi amahirwe yo gukoresha imodoka mu buryo bwateguwe, gukora transport no kubona amafaranga, mu gihe agenda yegera intego yo kuzagira imodoka ye bwite, hakurikijwe amasezerano agirana na MGK. Icyitonderwa: Ingwate/deposit, uburyo bwo kwishyura, igihe cy’amasezerano n’ibindi bisabwa bizasobanurwa neza ku bakandida bujuje ibisabwa mbere yo gutangira gahunda. Cyangwa kuba uzi : Kumenyekanisha gahunda ya Gupatana mu bice bitandukanye bya Kigali. Gushaka no kwegera abashoferi bashobora kwitabira gahunda. Gukoresha WhatsApp n’imbuga nkoranyambaga mu kumenyekanisha amahirwe ya MGK. Kugeza kuri MGK amakuru y’abifuza kwitabira gahunda. Gufasha mu bikorwa byo kwamamaza no kwegera abakiriya cyangwa abakozi bashya. Kumenyekanisha MGK n’ibikorwa byayo. Umuntu ushakishwa Turashaka umuntu: Ufite ubushobozi bwo kuvugana n’abantu neza. Ukoresha neza WhatsApp n’imbuga nkoranyambaga. Ufite umuhate kandi ukunda gushaka ibisubizo. Ushobora gukora neza atagomba guhora akurikiranwa. Ushishikajwe na Marketing, Sales, Transport cyangwa Entrepreneurship. Uzi neza Kigali n’abantu bahatuye. Uburambe muri Marketing cyangwa Sales ni inyongera, ariko si ngombwa. KUKI WAKWIFATANYA NA MGK? Amahirwe yo kwinjira muri gahunda ya Gupatana. Amahirwe yo kubona uburambe mu bijyanye na Transport na Marketing. Gukorera muri gahunda ifite amabwiriza n’amasezerano asobanutse. Amahirwe yo kwagura imiyoboro y’akazi n’ubucuruzi. Amahirwe yo gukorana n’ikigo gikora mu rwego rwa transport n’imicungire y’imodoka mu Kigali. UKO WASABA Abifuza kwitabira amahirwe ya Gupatana Driver cyangwa kuba Marketing Volunteer basabwe kohereza ubusabe bwabo kuri: Email:mgkltd26@gmail.com Aho ibikorwa bibera: Kigali, Rwanda Uko wandika ku busabe Ku bashoferi: andika “GUPATANA DRIVER” Ku ba Marketing Volunteers: andika “MARKETING VOLUNTEER” MGK Dufasha abantu kubona amahirwe binyuze muri Transport. Apply

title: Territory Lead
experience_raw: Mid career (3 to 5 years of experience)
raw_text: JOB DESCRIPTION: TERRITORY LEAD Company: EarthEnable Reports to: District Operations Lead Location: Different districts in Rwanda Compensation: 320,000 - 350,000 RWF (Rwandan Franc) / month gross, depending on experience Who We Are At EarthEnable, we believe that our clients deserve our very best, that work should be fun, and that the best ideas could come from any part of the company. We celebrate each other’s wins, learn from our setbacks, and are deeply proud of the impact we make every day. We believe a home that doesn’t make you sick means more than living disease-free. It means pride and dignity in the place our customers most treasure: their homes. Being a part of our team means more than building housing products: it means building an organization and building a better future for rural families. What We Do EarthEnable is transforming the way people live, by making homes healthier for families across rural Rwanda, Uganda, and Kenya. 80% of Rwandans live in homes with dirt floors which are dusty, unsanitary, and fertile breeding grounds for parasites and germs. While replacing a dirt floor with concrete has significant health benefits (e.g. reducing diarrhea by 50% and parasitic infections by 80%), concrete is unaffordable for many who need it, and is also responsible for 8% of global carbon emissions. EarthEnable addresses this pressing and ubiquitous problem by selling high-quality, earthen housing products like our flagship floor that is 80% cheaper than concrete with 90% less embedded energy. Earthen floors, plasters, and blocks are composed of natural materials (gravel, clay, sand, and laterite) and sealed with a proprietary drying oil that makes them waterproof, strong, and polished. In our first decade of operations, EarthEnable has installed ~60,000 products for over 300,000 individuals and created livelihoods for over 1,300 people. See our new product - a full house - here! Position Overview The Territory Lead is responsible for the overall performance, growth, and operational excellence of their assigned territory. This role combines commercial leadership, operational oversight, and people management to ensure sales targets are met, construction projects are executed efficiently, and customers receive an exceptional experience. The ideal candidate is a proactive and results-driven leader who can translate strategy into execution, build high-performing teams, and operate with strong business acumen in dynamic field environments. Key Responsibilities 1. Territory Ownership and Business Performance Own the end-to-end performance of the territory, ensuring alignment with company growth objectives and operational priorities. Develop and execute localized sales and operational strategies informed by market insights, customer needs, and competitive dynamics. Drive achievement of assigned sales and build targets while maintaining strong quality and customer satisfaction standards. Monitor territory performance through data and KPIs, proactively identifying risks and implementing corrective actions. 2. Sales Leadership and Customer Experience Lead the recruitment, onboarding, training, and ongoing development of Customer Sales Officers (CSOs) to build a strong and productive sales force. Equip teams with the tools, messaging, and support needed to effectively engage customers and convert leads. Champion customer-centric practices, ensuring a seamless journey from initial engagement through project completion. Strengthen relationships with cooperatives, institutions, local leaders, and community stakeholders to expand market reach and reinforce EarthEnable’s mission. Oversee territory-level marketing and activation initiatives to drive demand and brand visibility. 3. Operational and Construction Excellence Oversee all construction activities within the territory, ensuring adherence to quality standards, timelines, and safety practices. Align construction capacity with sales volume to prevent project delays and backlog. Partner closely with operations teams to coordinate material forecasting, ordering, and delivery. Track project progress and ensure timely follow-up on active builds, addressing bottlenecks before they escalate. Continuously identify opportunities to improve construction efficiency and reduce cycle times. 4. Financial Stewardship and Data Integrity Ensure customer payments are collected in accordance with company policies while maintaining the highest standards of financial accountability. Monitor territory-level financial indicators, including revenue, cost drivers, and operational efficiency. Promote accurate and timely data capture to support reporting, forecasting, and informed decision-making. Safeguard company resources by reinforcing compliance with internal controls. 5. Team Leadership and Culture Building Build, lead, and retain a high-performing territory team across sales and construction functions. Provide regular coaching, mentorship, and structured performance feedback to strengthen capability and accountability. Foster a culture grounded in professionalism, collaboration, continuous learning, and results. Model EarthEnable’s values and cultivate an environment where team members feel motivated, supported, and empowered to succeed. Qualifications and Experience Bachelor’s degree in Business, Sales, Operations, or a related field. Minimum of 3+ years of progressive experience in field operations, sales leadership, or territory management. Demonstrated success managing teams and delivering measurable business results. Strong operational mindset with the ability to balance commercial growth and execution quality. Experience working in fast-paced or growth-oriented organizations is highly desirable. Proficiency in data-driven decision-making and performance management. Key Competencies Strong leadership and people development skills Results-oriented with high ownership and accountability Strategic thinker with strong execution capability Excellent stakeholder and community engagement skills Financial and operational discipline Adaptability and resilience in dynamic environments Clear communicator with the ability to influence and motivate teams Application link Apply

experience_raw: Entry level (1 to 3 years of experience)
raw_text: Rwanda Ultimate Golf Course Ltd Job Description Title: F&B Cashier Reports to: F&B Supervisor / F&B Manager Education level : Diploma or certificate in Hospitality, Accounting, or Business Administration. Job Purpose: Rwanda Ultimate Golf Course is a private company created to position Rwanda as the best golfing destination in Africa and one of the greatest in the world. The first project of Rwanda Ultimate Golf Course, in order to reach this goal, is the Kigali Golf Resort & Villas. The golf course is a real estate masterpiece designed by the worldwide famous Gary Player. The facility will also include a five-star Clubhouse and other amenities. The F&B Cashier is responsible for handling all payment transactions within the Food & Beverage outlets of Rwanda Ultimate Golf Course Ltd, including restaurants, bars, lounges, and poolside outlets. The role ensures accurate billing, secure handling of cash and credit card transactions, and adherence to company financial and service standards. The F&B Cashier works closely with service staff and management to provide smooth, efficient, and professional guest experience. Responsibilities include but not limited to: Accurately process all guest bills in accordance with RUGC’s policies and service standards. Operate the MICROS POS system for posting and settling guest checks. Handle multiple forms of payment: cash, credit/debit cards, membership accounts, Etc. Verify guest bills before settlement to ensure accuracy in pricing, taxes, and discounts. Issue receipts to guests and obtain necessary signatures where applicable. Open and close cashier shifts in the MICROS POS system as per standard operating procedures. Maintain proper float and ensure all transactions balance at the end of the shift. Prepare accurate cash summaries, deposit slips, and daily cashier reports. Immediately report any discrepancies or irregularities to the F&B Supervisor or F&B Manager. Ensure safekeeping of all cash, vouchers, and receipts during the shift. Ensure all transactions are recorded in the system in real-time and in the correct outlet category. Record and reconcile any complimentary, voided, or discounted items with proper authorization. Maintain organized files for cashier reports, shift summaries, and signed guest checks. Support the F&B Office in preparing daily revenue reports and coordinating with Finance for audit purposes. Provide courteous and efficient service to guests during billing and payment. Respond professionally to billing inquiries and resolve issues promptly. Work in coordination with the service team to ensure guest satisfaction and smooth operations. Adhere to all financial, accounting, and control procedures set by RUGC and the Finance Department. Ensure compliance with company policies on discounts, promotions, and complimentary transactions. Follow cash handling procedures strictly to prevent loss or fraud. Maintain confidentiality of financial data and guest information. Work closely with the F&B Supervisors, Waitstaff, and Outlet Managers to support smooth operations. Coordinate with the Finance team during daily cash drops and audits. Assist in training new cashiers or service staff on billing procedures as required. Qualifications: A1 Diploma or certificate in Hospitality, Accounting, or Business Administration. Bachelor’s degree will be an added advantage Minimum 2 years of experience as a cashier in a 4- or 5-star hotel, resort, or luxury restaurant. Experience in using MICROS POS or similar point-of-sale systems. Basic knowledge of accounting and cash-handling procedures. Strong numerical accuracy and attention to detail. Key Competencies: Excellent customer service and interpersonal skills. High integrity and sense of responsibility. Accuracy and attention to detail in financial transactions. Ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced environment. Good communication and teamwork skills. Familiarity with hospitality systems and basic computer proficiency. Required documents: A detailed CV with 3 contacts of professional referees. A one-page cover letter with a motivation statement in relation to the responsibilities and requirements for this position. Copies of academic degree, professional training certificates, and other relevant training certificates. A copy of your national ID How to Apply The deadline for submitting applications is Monday, September 14, 2026, at 17:00 hrs Kigali time. All applicants must send their zipped documents to hr@kigaligolf.rw with the subject line " F&B Cashier Position." Only selected candidates for interview will be contacted. Apply

experience_raw: Senior (5+ years of experience)
raw_text: Job Description Job Title: Peri-operative nurse Department: Clinical Services Grade: Location: Burera District Reports to: HoD Clinical Services Positions reporting to: N/A Main Responsibilities 1 Job Purpose The Perioperative Nurse provides safe, high-quality, evidence-based nursing care to patients undergoing surgical and invasive procedures. Working within a multidisciplinary surgical team, the nurse is responsible for preoperative assessment and preparation, intraoperative patient advocacy and support, and postoperative monitoring and care. The position also contributes to clinical teaching, mentorship of nursing staff and students, and continuous quality improvement to ensure patient safety and adherence to perioperative standards and protocols. 2 Specific Responsibilities: Clinical nursing care Develop, implement, and evaluate perioperative nursing care plans in collaboration with the surgical and multidisciplinary team across preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative phases. Conduct comprehensive preoperative patient assessments and ensure readiness for surgery, including verification of consent, investigations, and safety checklists. Monitor patients’ vital signs and intraoperative parameters, responding promptly to changes in condition and escalating concerns to the surgical or anesthesia team. Assist surgeons, anesthetists, and other healthcare providers during surgical procedures, ensuring aseptic technique and patient safety in the operating theatre. Provide safe and effective postoperative nursing care, including pain management, wound care, drain management, and early detection of surgical complications. Educate patients and families on perioperative processes, surgical procedures, recovery expectations, and post-discharge care instructions. Ensure accurate, timely, and complete perioperative documentation, including surgical safety checklists and intraoperative records, in line with hospital standards and protocols. Patient Safety & Quality Improvement Participate in perioperative adverse event reporting and root cause analysis processes in compliance with hospital patient safety and surgical quality standards. Contribute to operating theatre continuous quality improvement initiatives, including surgical audits, infection prevention reviews, and perioperative outcome monitoring. Adhere to Rwanda Hospital Accreditation Standards and support operating theatre preparedness for accreditation assessments and surgical safety compliance. Ensure proper use, sterilization, maintenance, and inventory management of surgical instruments, anesthesia equipment, and theatre supplies; report any deficiencies to the theatre in charge. Report surgical incidents, adverse events, and near misses promptly in line with hospital policies and perioperative safety reporting systems. Teaching, Mentorship & Professional Development Mentor and support orientationf of new staff and students during clinical rotations on the ward. Participate in ward-based in-service training, case presentations, and nursing grand rounds. Engage in continuing professional development (CPD) activities and apply new knowledge to clinical practice. Support the implementation of evidence-based nursing practice guidelines and standard operating procedures (SOPs). Collaboration & Communication Participate actively in daily team rounds, handover reports, and care coordination meetings. Communicate effectively with patients, families, and team members, maintaining dignity, confidentiality, and cultural sensitivity. Required Qualifications Master of science in peri-operative nursing with a valid nursing license of practing in Rwanda Minimum of 5 years of clinical nursing experience in perioperative or surgical nursing in a hospital setting; experience in a teaching or referral hospital is an added value. Demonstrated experience in clinical teaching, mentorship, and supervision of nursing staff and students in the operating theatre environment. Familiarity with Rwanda national clinical protocols, infection prevention and control (IPC) standards, and surgical safety checklist systems. Strong clinical assessment, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills in perioperative patient management. Proficiency in basic computer skills and willingness to use electronic medical record and theatre documentation systems. Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary surgical and anesthesia team. Ability to support basic data collection, quality improvement tracking, and perioperative outcome analysis. Fluent in English and Kinyarwanda; knowledge of French is an advantage. Ability to live PIH/IMB values: Ubumuntu-Compassion, Ubupfura-Integrity, Ubunyangamugayo-Honesty, Ubwubahane-Mutual respect, Ubufatanye-Solidarity, Agaciro-Dignity, Kugira ishyaka-Determination. raw_text: GEOLOGIST – MINING Company: Lyon Mining Services Ltd Location: Rwanda – Based in Kigali with regular travel to mining sites Reporting to: Technical Director Employment Type: Full-time Positions: 2 About Us Lyon Mining Services Ltd is a Rwanda-based mining consulting company providingspecialized technical and operational support to mining projects. Our services include mine surveying, underground and surface 3D SLAM/LiDARscanning, geological consulting, mining engineering, mine planning and design, digital mining solutions, and mine management support. We combine experienced technical professionals with modern technologies to helpmining companies improve safety, productivity, accuracy, operational control, anddecision-making. Our goal is to contribute to the development of a mining industry that is smarter, more productive, and globally competitive. The Role Lyon Mining Services Ltd is seeking a motivated and technically competent Mining Geologist to join our technical team. The Geologist will support geological activities across various mining and explorationprojects, including geological mapping, sampling, logging, mineral identification, grade control, geological data collection and interpretation, resource evaluation, and geological reporting. The position involves regular fieldwork at mining and exploration sites across Rwanda and close collaboration with mining engineers, surveyors, processing teams, mine operators, and clients. Key Responsibilities Conduct geological mapping, sampling, logging, and mineral identification at mining andexploration sites. Support grade control, orebody interpretation, and geological data collection. Prepare geological maps, sections, sampling records, and technical reports. Interpret geological and assay data to support mine planning and production activities. Assist with exploration, resource evaluation, and geological modelling. Collaborate with mining, survey, processing, and operational teams. Maintain accurate geological databases, sample records, and field documentation. Ensure compliance with health, safety, environmental, and professional standards. Requirements Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Applied Geology, Mining Geology, Earth Sciences, or a related field. Practical knowledge of mining or exploration geology. Good understanding of geological mapping, sampling, logging, grade control, and mineral identification. Ability to interpret geological and assay data and prepare clear technical reports. Familiarity with GIS, geological, CAD, or mine-planning software is an advantage. Strong analytical, communication, teamwork, and fieldwork skills. Willingness to travel regularly and work at mining sites across Rwanda. Good command of English; knowledge of Kinyarwanda and/or French is an advantage. What We Offer Opportunity to work on a variety of mining, exploration, and geological consulting projects. Exposure to both underground and surface mining operations. Opportunity to work alongside mining engineers, surveyors, geologists, and other technical specialists. Exposure to modern mining and digital technologies, including SLAM/LiDARscanning, GNSS surveying, drone surveying, 3D mine visualization, and geological data integration. Continuous professional development and practical field experience. A dynamic working environment with opportunities for increased technical and professional responsibility. Competitive remuneration based on qualifications, experience, and demonstrated capability. title: Finance Officer
experience_raw: Mid career (3 to 5 years of experience)
raw_text: RWANDA WOMEN'S NETWORK (RWN) TERMS OF REFERENCE FINANCE OFFICER (1 POSITION) Project: Empowered Civil Society: Enhancing Capacity and Transparency for Gender Equality in Rwanda Position title Finance Officer Number of positions 1 (one) Reports to Finance Manager Works closely with Project Coordinator, Logistics and Procurement Officer, Administrative Assistant, and partner CSO finance staff Duty station RWN Head Office, Kigali, with periodic field travel to partner CSOs Contract type Full-time, fixed-term (renewable annually, subject to performance and funding availability) Project duration 1 July 2026 – 30 June 2029 (36 months) Funded by Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (SIDA) 1. Background Rwanda Women's Network (RWN) is implementing a three-year project, funded by Sida, aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity and transparency of RWN and selected local, women-led civil society organizations (CSOs), and enhancing their collaboration with government and other stakeholders at district and national levels. The project channels a significant share of its budget as sub-grants to nine (9) partner CSOs, making strong financial management, internal control, and compliance systems essential. RWN is recruiting a full-time Finance Officer to work alongside the part-time Finance Manager, forming a dual financial management structure that strengthens internal control and risk mitigation across the project, including oversight of sub-granted funds. 2. Purpose of the Position The Finance Officer is responsible for day-to-day financial operations of the project, including financial tracking and documentation, verification of partner CSO financial reports, and support to budgeting, disbursement, and audit processes. The role ensures accurate, timely, and compliant financial management in line with RWN's financial policies and Sida's requirements. 3. Key Responsibilities Financial Tracking, Documentation and Record-Keeping Maintain accurate and up-to-date financial records, ledgers, and supporting documentation for all project transactions. Process payments, advances, and reimbursements in line with RWN's financial procedures and approval thresholds. Reconcile bank statements, cash accounts, and project ledgers on a regular basis. Maintain an organized, audit-ready filing system (physical and electronic) for all financial records. Sub-Grant Financial Management and CSO Support Verify the accuracy, completeness, and eligibility of expenditures submitted by partner CSOs against approved budgets and supporting documents (voucher review). Support partner CSOs to apply sound financial management and reporting practices, including through onboarding, training, and ongoing hands-on support. Track disbursement schedules and follow up on phased release of sub-grant funds tied to verified reporting and results. Participate in quarterly financial monitoring visits to partner CSOs, including spot checks and verification of financial documentation. Flag discrepancies, ineligible expenditures, or irregularities to the Finance Manager and Project Coordinator, and support corrective action. Budgeting and Financial Reporting Support the Finance Manager in preparing and monitoring the project budget, including budget-versus-actual analysis. Consolidate financial data from RWN and partner CSOs to support timely and accurate financial reports to RWN management and Sida. raw_text: Job Description-Senior Breast Imaging Officer/ for R01-MURIKA Project Job Title: Senior Breast Imaging Officer Departments: Clinical and Research Grade: 4B Location: Butaro, with frequent travels to other selected intervention sites Duration of Contract: September 2026 – April 2030 renewable upon availability of funds Reports to: -Director of Research and Training Organization Profile 1 In 2005, PIH and its Rwandan sister organization, Inshuti Mu Buzima (IMB), began working in partnership with the government of Rwanda to address the HIV/AIDS epidemic afflicting the population and to comprehensively strengthen the public health system in rural, underserved districts in Rwanda. Today, PIH/IMB supports delivery of comprehensive integrated non-communicable disease (NCD) services in three rural districts of Rwanda, including cancer care. Cancer care is predominantly based at the flagship Butaro Cancer Center of Excellence (BCCOE), which was inaugurated in June 2012 and has since provided care to over 9,000 patients, with services ranging from cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.As breast cancer incidence rises in Rwanda, innovative and sustainable strategies to facilitate timely, accurate diagnoses are urgently needed to eliminate these preventable deaths. High-quality breast imaging is essential for the evaluation of potential cancer. Specifically, diagnostic breast ultrasound is the global standard of care in evaluating breast masses and more accurate than physical exam alone in identifying benign versus malignant disease. By triaging lesions requiring biopsy, ultrasound may also reduce unnecessary referrals and allocate resources to those most likely to have cancer. However, radiologists are still scarce and breast ultrasound is typically offered only at urban referral hospitals. Decentralizing breast ultrasound to district hospitals would expand access to this critical evidence-based intervention, particularly for low-income rural patients facing heightened barriers to referral hospital care. It is with this regards that Rwandan policymakers have called for breast ultrasound decentralization at all district hospitals. Based on this, PIH/IMB in collaboration with Brigham and Women’s Hospital(BWH) are implementing a project entitled “MURIKA (Mobilizing Ultrasound for Breast Imaging and Care)” aiming to use a fully powered hybrid implementation-effectiveness trial design, to examine whether real-time virtual supervision using teleultrasound technology is more effective than asynchronous virtual feedback in facilitating breast ultrasound provision and maintaining clinicians’ skills at 16 Rwandan selected district hospitals. During the tele-ultrasound supervision, the trained clinicians/medical imaging technologists will receive real time supervision and feedback from the incumbent Senior Breast Imaging Officer on a video call using REACTS (a radiology software). For asynchronous virtual supervision, the clinicians-trainees will save the ultrasound images and will be shared with the incumbent who will provide them feedback within 24 hours. The project will focus on comparing the effectiveness of these two strategies in terms of building the trainees’ skills and supporting the incorporation of the breast ultrasound provision into clinical care at the 16 district hospitals. 2 Overall Responsibilities:Under the guidance of PIH/IMB Research and Training and Oncology Programs Leadership, as well as BWH partners, the Senior Breast Imaging Officer will be mainly responsible for leading clinical interventions, trainings, mentorship and supervision in diagnostic breast ultrasound within the 16 selected intervention hospitals and PIH/IMB supported sites, following the established radiology requirements and regulations to ensure patient care, safety and clinicians’ skills enhancement. The position will also be involved in different related research activities, expert meetings, workshops, and curriculum reviews. Specific Responsibilities and Duties: Developing diagnostic breast ultrasound training curricula; Leading breast ultrasound trainings, combining in-person and web-based didactic lectures and supervision; Supporting the assessments of the effectiveness of the training and supervision strategies; Serving as a virtual mentor-supervisor for the selected study or intervention sites/hospitals (via tele-ultrasound for some hospitals and asynchronous supervision for other sites); Participating in regular (weekly, monthly, quarterly) meetings and workshops with different stakeholders; Supporting study results interpretation, dissemination and translation of findings into policy and practice; Providing clinical expertise on diagnostic breast ultrasound while supporting other breast medical imaging project-related activities as needed and requested by the PIH/IMB supervisors. Ideal Qualifications, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Bachelor’s degree in Medical Imaging Services; a Master’s degree being an added advantage; Having worked in cancer control or breast cancer early detection national programs; Working specialization in medical breast imaging techniques and equipment, especially in diagnostic breast ultrasound; 3-5 years’ experience in imaging services from a reputable health/ radiology institution/center Some experience with a CT Scan, MRI and mammography machines is also an added advantage; Flexibility and willingness to work across several locations, in resource limited settings, including rural areas and diverse team ; Strong management, communication, mentoring, teaching and leadership skills; Highly organized and able to manage a heavy patient load; Have compassion for vulnerable population, advocacy for their well-being and medical needs; Persuaded and practicing the principles of equity; Showing expert skills, knowledge, experience and passion for medical imaging techniques especially in diagnostic breast ultrasound; Ability to live PIH/IMB values: Ubumuntu-Compassion, Ubupfura-Integrity, Ubunyangamugayo-Honesty, Ubwubahane-Mutual respect, Ubufatanye-Solidarity, Agaciro-Dignity, Kugira ishyaka-Determination. title: Safety, Security and Safeguarding Coordinator

raw_text: Save the Children has been working in Rwanda since 1994 in partnership with the Government of Rwanda and local stakeholders to promote a bright future for children, with experience working in all 30 districts of the country. The post holder will also be expected to provide significant mentoring and capacity-building to Save the Children’s staff, volunteers, suppliers, consultants, associates and partners. The role holder will work in conjunction with the Country Senior Leadership Team and Safeguarding focal persons located across Rwanda and Burundi. The post- holder will be working closely with the Regional Security Director (RSD) in carrying out safety and security assessments; make recommendations and provide support for their implementation by Country Office. She/ He will facilitate the implementation of Save the Children’s Safety and Security Policy and Standards within country programs and help drive systemic change in the quality of safety and security management. Undertake clear, strong advocacy in line with the Safeguarding Policies at National levels. Safe programming and Safeguarding Practice promoted across Rwanda and Burundi offices Work with programme development team and other programme staff to ensure that all programming is designed, implemented and monitored through a Safeguarding lens, including supporting all new proposals Ensure that support for safeguarding is adequately resourced in all new project budgets Support staff to take proactive steps to ensure that all programming activity identifies the potential risks and works to eliminate and mitigate those risks. Ensure that the tools and knowledge are made available to managers and that they know how to access support and guidance Role model high levels of professional safeguarding behaviour and maintain the standards required by the Safeguarding Policies and Code of Conduct Country roll-out and maintenance of training programmes Deliver a suite of mandatory core training workshops so as to enable staff with key responsibilities to undertake their roles and mainstream safeguarding functions Deliver on-going refresher training and safeguarding inductions as appropriate Review and strengthen Safeguarding systems within the country office, planning, and delivering training programs accordingly. Identify Safeguarding issues within Save the Children operational areas and develop a plan to respond to them in collaboration with other internal and external partners Deploy resources of the Keeping Children Safe strategically to ensure that the country office, its partners and all representatives maintain Save the Children safeguarding standards. Capacity Building Develop capacity building plan for staff and partners and provide on-going mentoring and support Serve as safeguarding lead focal point for the field office and lead on establishment of strong safeguarding procedures and risk assessment in all programme activities in accordance with the national strategies developed Build the capacity of Safeguarding Focal points to deliver safeguarding trainings, manage & undertake investigation Build the capacity of Safeguarding focal persons especially in receiving and recording reports Strengthen the capacity of Focal points in delivering safeguarding inductions With the support of the safety and Security RO, develop and deliver training modules specific to knowledge gaps within the CO Safety and Security team (SSFP) to improve safety and security capacity. Identify gaps within the Field Offices in security management and planning and help resource improvements. Safeguarding Standards are applied throughout the country programme Coordinate with the Senior Leadership Team and monitor the overall implementation of safeguarding policies in the country programme. Conduct a review of safeguarding policy implementation throughout the country programme and implement the Safeguarding Policy Compliance Action Plan Ensure that the safeguarding mechanisms are in place and are subject to continuous monitoring/review. Oversee and enforce follow-up in order to ensure maximum levels of compliance and competence. Identify and utilise opportunities to integrate safeguarding approaches into all aspects of our work Apply critical analysis to ensure that we live up to our commitment to making Save the Children safe for children by ensuring child safeguarding concerns are reported effectively in line with the policy, Work with the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) team to ensure that safeguarding and reporting are central to our accountability system for all projects Ensure that reporting procedures are clearly understood by staff, partners, contractors/suppliers, visitors and by children themselves. This may include providing briefings, training or developing materials for dissemination, including the development of child-friendly materials; Ensure that concerns are followed up safely, effectively and efficiently and to the required standards. Ensure that safeguarding concerns are documented and regularly analyzed to inform organizational learning and improve safeguarding practice; Analyze the types of cases received, and the response provided on a regular basis to inform organizational learning and improve safeguarding practice; Provide guidance Where appropriate, personally undertaking safeguarding investigations, sometimes in challenging environments and to rigorous timescales and standards. Collaborating with key teams and processes within the country office to ensure that Safeguarding is integrated into all systems Safety and Security responsibilities Assess threat, risk, and vulnerability and make recommendations to SMT to reduce staff exposure. Undertake safety and security assessments of program areas and potential program areas as requested by CD /SMT. Report on findings and design necessary improvements. Oversee assessment of SCI and international staff premises’ locations on regular basis and advice on any possible security measures or change of locations. Undertake reviews of individual safety and security procedures and policies as requested and make recommendations to SMT. Assist to the CD to prepare/maintain/update safety and security management plan (SSMP). Ensure staff training/orientation re: safety and security roles. Facilitate safety and security management training with staff in the country office and in project locations. Develop Security briefing materials for new staff and visitors. Provide security orientation/briefing for newly appointed SC staff and CO visitors. Ensure all SC staff understand and comply with incident reporting requirements and procedures. Follow-up as necessary re: issues related to reported incidents. Ensure that appropriate systems are in place to effectively disseminate safety and security information and updates of the security situation to SC staff. Conduct security awareness training in accordance with SCI policies and procedures and in cooperation with the Regional Security team Oversee assessment of SCI and international staff premises’ locations on regular basis and advice on any possible security measures or change of locations. Procedures and Protocols: Redundancy in communication is ensured by establishing multiple modes of communication between base and all offices in the field. Communications: Ensure that effective communications are in place including communication tree system, mobile phones etc All staff ‘communication tree’ is established and kept updated so as to contact all staff when necessary. Act in a Crisis: Support the Field Senior Management Teams (SMT) and advise them of possible actions or options in a time of crisis or emergency. Coordinate information through the relevant reporting lines during serious security incidents. Assist with emergency evacuations in coordination with the Regional Security Director Investigate and follow up security incidents Report security incidents in accordance with SCI protocols and using the online reporting system in timely manner. COMPETENCIES AND BEHAVIOURS Leading and Inspiring Others (Accomplished) Communicates our vision, values and strategy and encourages others to share them Influences others positively to achieve team goals Recognise and celebrates the contribution and success of individuals and the team Takes a flexible and positive leadership style, adapting to the situation or needs of the team Demonstrates humility in leadership of others Values, and articulates a compelling vision to inspire others to achieve our goals for children. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE Essential A Child Protection or Child Rights Governance professional with a degree in child protection, governance, law, social work.
